effects: Deploys a new BlueBuyCallback contract through CREATE2 with the given salt, or returns the existing one for (owner, salt); nothing is deployed twice.
The new callback contract makes `owner` its OWNER and authorizes `owner` on Morpho Blue to manage the callback's Blue positions.
The factory records the callback in callbackOf[owner][salt] and marks it in isBlueBuyCallback.
No token, ETH or approval of the signer moves; the function is not payable; the signer pays gas only.
formats.shown: The screen says "Create buy callback for <owner>" and shows the Owner address; the salt is hidden.

findings.title: createBlueBuyCallback intent "Create buy callback" does not say it deploys a contract owned by owner.
findings.evidence: BlueBuyCallbackFactory.createBlueBuyCallback: `address(new BlueBuyCallback{salt: salt}(owner, MIDNIGHT, BLUE))`; the BlueBuyCallback constructor calls `IMorpho(BLUE).setAuthorization(OWNER, true)`. The descriptor has intent "Create buy callback" and interpolatedIntent "Create buy callback for {#.owner}". In both cases the blind reader lists as unsure "What a 'buy callback' actually does" and whether it can spend their tokens.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Deploy Morpho buy callback contract" and the interpolatedIntent to "Deploy Morpho buy callback contract owned by {#.owner}".

cases.notes: The mined tx has no token or ETH effects. The screen correctly shows the owner, who is the signer here. The reader understood the owner correctly.

The mined tx has no effects on the signer. The owner differs from the signer and the screen shows that owner. The reader correctly saw that nothing leaves the wallet and that the owner is another address.
